title: artifact-version-delta-investigation-notes
content:
Quick notes + command history while debugging the canary rollback yesterday. Trying to keep a small searchable trail for follow-ups and postmortem.

Problem summary (short):
- Canary (canary-167) started failing perf checks ~2026-02-16 03:40 UTC after deploy of release v2026-02-16.3.
- Automated rollback triggered but service outage spike observed during rollback window.
- Hypothesis: artifact tag/promotion mismatch between CI artifact store and registry (image tag points to different digest than the one pulled by canary instances).

What I saw in console (rough timeline):
- 03:38 UTC: CI job release/push succeeded: artifact published to s3://redwood-artifacts/releases/v2026-02-16.3/release.tar.gz (md5: 5d9f3c4e)
- 03:40 UTC: Canary healthchecks start failing (increased latency, 502s from nginx frontends)
- 03:42 UTC: Orchestrator (k8s controller) starts evicting canary pods -> new pods pulling image redwood/release:v2026-02-16.3
- 03:43 UTC: Image pull succeeded but init failed: extracting binary -> mismatch checksum reported by our post-extract integrity check (exit 1)
- 03:45 UTC: Rollback-to-last-stable triggered (v2026-02-10.9)
- 03:47 UTC: Some nodes still had mixed artifacts -> transient 503s

Commands I ran (copy-paste-ish):
- aws s3 ls s3://redwood-artifacts/releases/v2026-02-16.3/ --recursive
  -> found release.tar.gz and manifest.json
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/releases/v2026-02-16.3/manifest.json - | jq .
  -> manifest sha256: a3c2b1... (reported by CI)
- docker pull registry.redwood:5000/release:v2026-02-16.3
- docker inspect --format='{{.RepoDigests}}' registry.redwood:5000/release:v2026-02-16.3
  -> repoDigest: registry.redwood:5000/release@sha256:8f6a9b...
- skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood:5000/release:v2026-02-16.3
  -> remote digest: sha256:8f6a9b... (expected)
- ssh node-07
  sudo journalctl -u release-canary -n 200 | sed -n '1,120p'
  -> post-extract integrity check failed: expected sha256 a3c2b1..., got sha256 b72d1f...

Error snippets captured:
- "integrity-check: mismatch: expected a3c2b1..., computed b72d1...\nexiting"
- "kubernetes: container init failed: exit code 1"
- nginx upstream 502: "upstream prematurely closed connection"

Observed artifact mismatch details (notes):
- CI manifest.json references a packaged binary with sha256 a3c2b1..., but the container image contains binary with sha256 b72d1f... (different). Two possibilities:
  1) Image build used an older/alternate artifact from local cache instead of the S3 object. (race/CI cache)
  2) Tag v2026-02-16.3 was re-used / re-tagged after initial push and image registry entry points to a different digest.
  3) Our S3 replication (eu->us) lag caused the image builder to pick a partially uploaded artifact (unlikely but possible if builder doesn't handle eventual consistency correctly).

What we verified quickly:
- Rebuilt the image locally from s3 artifact pulled explicitly (sha256 a3c2b1...): produced digest sha256:8f6a9b... -> matches registry digest for tag v2026-02-16.3
- Pulled the image from registry on node-07 (where failure occurred) and extracted binary inside image: binary checksum b72d1f... -> mismatch.
- registry API shows two pushes for tag v2026-02-16.3 within 5 minutes window (see registry logs)

Hypothesis refinement:
- Likely scenario: CI pipeline did an initial build and pushed image A (digest 8f6a9b...) and published S3 manifest referencing artifact A. Then, a follow-up job (retry / force push from a different runner) pushed image B (digest b72d1f...) to the same tag v2026-02-16.3 without updating the S3 manifest (race). Our canary pods pulled image B due to registry's last-write-wins tag, but the manifest and checksum watchers expected A -> integrity check failed.

Quick checks to confirm:
- registry logs (grep for "PUT /v2/release/manifests/v2026-02-16.3") show two POSTs at 03:37:50 and 03:39:02 UTC from different runner IPs (10.27.x.y and 10.28.x.z)
- CI job history: build #984 (03:37) and build #985 (03:39) both reference same release branch and were triggered by push event. #985 is marked 'retry' from auto-retry policy.

Rollback details executed by SRE (notes):
- kubectl set image deployment/release release=registry.redwood:5000/release:v2026-02-10.9 --namespace=prod
- kubectl rollout status deployment/release
- verified canary stable checks pass after full revert (~03:52 UTC)
- followup: manual purge of tag v2026-02-16.3 from registry to prevent accidental pulls:
  - registry garbage-collect and then delete tag refs (coord with registry team)

Triage actions / unfinished TODOs (for postmortem):
- [ ] Add atomic promotion step in CI: publish artifact -> verify push -> create registry tag in one transaction (or use immutable tags with digests).
- [ ] Add pre-push lock for re-tagging same tag to prevent two runners racing to push same tag.
- [ ] Ensure CI manifests are written after image push completes and include digest (not just tag).
- [ ] Enhance our integrity-checker to accept digest-from-image and cross-check with manifest digest instead of soft tag compare.
- [ ] Backfill registry logs and associate with runner IDs for full audit (request from registry team).
- [ ] Add a small script to detect multiple pushes to same tag in a short window and alert.

Notes-to-self for follow-up commands (what I still want to run):
- curl -s -u admin:token "https://registry.redwood/v2/_catalog" | jq .
- docker pull registry.redwood:5000/release@sha256:8f6a9b...
- docker save | tar -tf - | grep release-binary || sha256sum release-binary
- query CI DB: SELECT * FROM builds WHERE release_tag='v2026-02-16.3' ORDER BY created_at DESC;
- ask build-team to dump runner environment for #985 (CACHE=true? local-cache path?)

Possible postmortem blurb (draft):
- Root cause: race condition in CI where a retry/push overwrote an already-published tag. The deployment pipeline relied on tag equality rather than image digest, causing canary to pull an image not matching the published manifest and fail integrity checks.
- Impact: Canary healthchecks failed and an automated rollback caused a short availability wobble. No customer data lost.
- Remediation: move to digest-pinned deployments for rollback endpoints, enforce single-writer tag policy, and drop immediate retries that re-tag the same release label.

Misc random observations:
- Node-07 had an older docker version; containerd pulled layers differently (did we hit a layering/caching bug?). Consider standardizing runtime image clean-up across fleet.
- The canary healthcheck was strict (binary checksum) which helped detect this. Low-latency detection saved us from wider rollout.

If I forget: ping @rhea and @tomas about running registry log export for 03:35-03:45 UTC window and ask build-team to reproduce with local cache off.

End of scratchpad. Keep this in users so it's easy for devs to find. Will convert to postmortem draft after registry logs and build runner dump are attached.
